contains: The following discussion sets forth the material risk factors that could affect JPMorganChase
The Consolidated Financial Statements, the Notes thereto and the report of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm

provenance: PR #45 R1 (2026-08-24), hard rule 2. JPM FY2024 10-K (iXBRL, EDGAR accession 0000019617-25-000270): every page carries the running head 'JPMorgan Chase & Co./2024 Form 10-K' and a page number typeset INSIDE a two-cell <table> (e.g. ADR-026 span {start: 218110, end: 218146, kind: running_head} inside the table block [218110, 218149) 'JPMorgan Chase & Co./2024 Form 10-K\n\n49'), so all 572 ADR-026 chrome runs of this filing lie inside table blocks and none is a whole block. ADR-031 §b4 as first shipped left a block out of the Markdown only when it lay WHOLLY inside a chrome span, so with exclude_boilerplate=True and blocks=True the rendered Markdown of the whole document carried 286 running heads (strip_chrome leaves 0) while the inspector's header said 'boilerplate hidden' (reviewer repro: to_markdown(omit=spans) == to_markdown() byte-for-byte). Watched RED at 0f194cf — see the red line in tasks/reviews/pr45-r1-resolution.json. The rule after the repair: chrome runs inside a block are removed from its rendered text exactly as boilerplate.strip_chrome removes them (paragraph/heading slices and table cells alike); a row or block left empty disappears. The un-omitted rendering must still carry the string (second check), so the case proves the omission and not a missing head; `min_chrome_runs` pins that the envelope carried at least 500 chrome runs into the render (572 at HEAD), and the `boilerplate` check that at least 250 of them are running heads (286 at HEAD). PR #45 R7 (round 2, 2026-08-24): the stripped checks were not_contains-only, so a renderer answering the empty string whenever omit is non-empty passed the whole gate (measured: fast 110/110, invariant 52/52 under `if omit: return ""`; only the markdown/view self-checks, which no gate runs, went red). Both omit_chrome checks now also assert a PRESERVED prose snippet via `contains`: the whole-document window pins item 1A's opening sentence ('The following discussion sets forth the material risk factors that could affect JPMorganChase', once in normalized_text at 47375) and the item-15 window pins the financial-statements sentence ('The Consolidated Financial Statements, the Notes thereto and the report of the Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm', once, at 201373, inside item 15's span). Neither snippet intersects any of the 572 ADR-026 spans (verified offset-against-span before labeling), so a correct strip keeps both and the empty-render mutation is red: `stripped markdown missing 'The following discussion sets forth ...'`.
